general_information.Description: The objective of the course is to help students apply the knowledge about data mining to apply in practice to solve problems to ensure requirements such as: - Use the discussed data mining techniques in practice, - Identify relevant data mining techniques from research articles for a given problem, - Formulate a methodological description on how a problem ought to be solved using data mining, - Analyse results and models from a data mining project. - Identify problems for which data mining is appropriate to use, - Select appropriate evaluation methods based on the data mining task at hand. - Learn about the legal and ethical aspects of data collection and use. - Analyze data mining problems and reason about the most appropriate methods to apply to a given dataset and knowledge extraction need. - Implement basic pre-processing, association mining, classification and clustering algorithms. - Apply and reflect on advanced pre-processing, association mining, classification and clustering algorithms. - Work efficiently in groups and evaluate the algorithms on real-world problems.
general_information.StudentTasks: # Choose appropriate project and form group. # Divide and schedule work among members. # Produce document and product according to project requirement and member work share. # Defend work infront of examination board, showing both project results and individual responsibility.
general_information.Tools: #Programming language: Python, R,… #Tools: Rapid Miner, Weka, Apache Spark #Database: o Kaggle: https://www.kaggle.com/ o Data Mining Cup: http://www.data-mining-cup.de o KDD Cup: https://www.kdd.org/kdd-cup
general_information.Note: Completion Criteria (in addition to grade criteria): * Students can prove that they create the product themselves * No fatal defect in software product (the students can't demonstrate)

general_information.Description: The course is to provide students knowledge about Data Warehouse technologies : - The need for Data Warehouse - Review formal definitions of a Data Warehouse - Data marts, metadata -Trends in Data Warehouse - Plan and Project management - Defining the business requirements - Requirement as the driving force for Data warehouse - The Architectural Components - Infrastructure as the Foundation for Data Warehousing - The Significant Role of Metadata - Dimensional Modeling - Data Extraction, Transformation, and Loading - Data Quality and Data Warehousing and the Web - Data Mining Basics - The Physical Design Process - Data Warehouse Deployment and Maintenance It also provides students oppotunities working on Microsoft SQL Server's Data warehousing Assessment scheme: 1) On-going asessment: - 1 Assignment: 30% - Lab activities 10% - 2 quizzes: 10x2= 20% 2) Final Exam: 40% 3) Final Result: 100% Completion Criteria: 1) Every on-going assessment component >0 2) Final Exam Score >=4 & Final Result >=5

general_information.Tools: Technical facilities: - Phần mềm Microsoft SQL Server

general_information.Description: The developing of cloud computing, big data, open source software, and improved algorithms kicked Artificial Intelligence (AI) into the mainstream of focus in technologies nowadays. AI technologies are fundamentally changing the ways we work, live, and manage businesses. This course is designed to present to student the coherent body of ideas and methods which were contributed to the development of Artificial Intelligence discipline. Student will be acquaint with the basic programs in the field and their underlying theory and will explore this through problem-solving paradigms, logic and theorem proving, language and image understanding, search and control methods and learning. This course aims to create following results on students: 1. Graduates will have ability to work with Tensor Flow machine learning library as a framework in developing AI their applications MO-1a: An ability to build models by plugging together building blocks with the user-friendly Keras sequential API. MO-1b: An ability to build models then write the forward and backward pass, create custom layers, activations, and training loops by using a define-by-run interface for customization and advanced research from Keras functional and subclassing APIs. 2. Graduates will have a broad understanding of the fundamental theories, concepts, and applications of Artificial Intelligence. MO-2a: An ability to apply knowledge of Artificial Intelligence appropriate to the discipline. MO-2b: An ability to analyze a problem and identify and define the AI requirements appropriate to its solution. MO-2c: An ability to design, implement, and evaluate an AI system to meet desired needs. 3. Graduates will be prepared for careers in Artificial Intelligence field. MO-3a: An ability to use current methodologies, techniques, skills, and tools necessary for AI practice. 4. Graduates will communicate effectively, both orally and in writing of Artificial Intelligence-related works. MO-4a: An ability to communicate effectively in AI-related works. MO-4b: An ability to discuss about how to control and to manage APIs of Tensor Flow library effectively.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend more than 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - use laptop in the class for learning purpose only - Constantly follow announcements on intranet/LMS athttps://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information regarding assignment submission and feedback on assignments

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Demonstrate working knowledge in Tensor Flow in order to write simple AI programs and explore more sophisticated Tensor Flow code on their own
Understand about Artificial Intelligence, its history and concepts such as Fuzzy Logic, Intelligent Agents, Machine Learning…
Understand different types of AI agents.
Know various AI search algorithms (uninformed, informed, constraint satisfaction, genetic algorithms)
Understand the fundamentals of knowledge representation (logic-based, frame-based, semantic nets), inference and theorem proving
Know how to build simple knowledge-based systems
Know some popular applications of Artificial Intelligence
Demonstrate working knowledge of reasoning in the presence of incomplete and/or uncertain information
Ability to apply knowledge representation, reasoning, and machine learning techniques to real-world problems
Ability to carry out works related to AI independently or collaborated with others and communicate effectively in a TensorFlow AI-related project setting.

general_information.Description: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed industries around the world, and has the potential to radically alter the field of healthcare. The aim of this unit is to introducethe current and future applications of AI in healthcare with the goal of learning to bring AI technologies into the clinic safely and ethically. Students will be guided to analyze data on patient, such as diseases, medications, tests, or valuable health information, and get a sense of how AI could transform patient care and diagnoses.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose - Promptly access to the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information

properties.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed industries around the world, and has the potential to radically alter the field of healthcare. The aim of this unit is to introducethe current and future applications of AI in healthcare with the goal of learning to bring AI technologies into the clinic safely and ethically. Students will be guided to analyze data on patient, such as diseases, medications, tests, or valuable health information, and get a sense of how AI could transform patient care and diagnoses.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Pre-process data and set up a pre-trained neural network.
Evaluate models by accuracy, specificity, predictive value, confidence intervals, ROC curve, and F1 score.
Diagnose diseases from x-rays and 3D MRI brain images.
Walk through examples of prognostic tasks.
Predict patient survival rates more accurately using tree-based models.
Navigate practical challenges in medicine, like missing data.
Estimate treatment effects on patients using data from randomized trials.
Explore methods to interpret diagnostic and prognostic models.
Automate the task of labeling medical datasets using natural language processing.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Understand the role of database and information systems security for enterprise and organization
Understand Security Architecture and plan defines steps to reinstate a network after a disaster occurs
Understand the steps of administrator must take into account prior to installation of a database Secure the installation and configuration of various database management systems
Understand the different database management system models and applications and describe the architecture of Oracle, MySQL, and Microsoft SQL Server
Understanding Secure the installation and configuration of MySQL server
Understanding Secure the installation and configuration of Microsoft SQL server
Understanding Secure the installation and configuration of Oracle
Understanding Password, Profiles, Privileges, and Roles with SQL Server, MySQL, and Oracle
Discover locate SQL vulnerabilities
Experience the case studies of hacking SQL injection
Understand common SQL statements and SQL constructs used to exploit weaknesses
Perform SQL injection exploitation and identify defensive strategies against these exploits
Understand of database auditing fundamentals
Perform the auditing activities that are specific to database security auditing
Understand the methodology used to perform a security test
Understand the remediation

general_information.Description: - This course introduces the key steps involved in the data mining pipeline, including data understanding, data preprocessing, data warehousing, data modeling, interpretation and evaluation, and real-world applications. - Students will learn the general concepts of data mining along with basic methodologies and applications. Then dive into one subfield in data mining: pattern discovery. Learn in-depth concepts, methods, and applications of pattern discovery in data mining. This courser will introduce methods for pattern-based classification and some interesting applications of pattern discovery. It also provides you the opportunity to learn skills and content to practice and engage in scalable pattern discovery methods on massive transactional data, discuss pattern evaluation measures, and study methods for mining diverse kinds of patterns, sequential patterns, and sub-graph patterns.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose - Promptly access to the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information
general_information.Note: Assignment: plus 0.5 to 1 points for completed Coursera certification, Final Result <=10

general_information.Description: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed industries around the world. The aim of this unit is to introduce the current and future applications of AI in trading strategy. Students will be guided to discover the structure used in machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and reinforcement learning (RL) techniques, the required steps, and the optimized methods in the AI-driven trading field. Students also learn how to build some ML models on Keras and Tensorflow.
general_information.StudentTasks: '- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose - Promptly access to the FU FLM at https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information

properties.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed industries around the world. The aim of this unit is to introduce the current and future applications of AI in trading strategy. Students will be guided to discover the structure used in machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and reinforcement learning (RL) techniques, the required steps, and the optimized methods in the AI-driven trading field. Students also learn how to build some ML models on Keras and Tensorflow.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Understand the fundamentals of trading.
Define quantitative trading and the main types of quantitative trading strategies.
Basic steps in exchange arbitrage, statistical arbitrage, index arbitrage and the application of machine learning to financial use cases.
Design basic quantitative trading strategies.
Use Keras and Tensorflow to build machine learning models.
Build a pair trading strategy prediction model, a momentum-based trading model, and back test them.
Understand the structure and techniques used in reinforcement learning (RL) strategies.
Understand the benefits of using RL vs. other learning methods.
Describe the steps required to develop, test, and optimize an RL trading strategy.

general_information.Syllabus Name: Nhạc cụ truyền thống - Đàn Bầu
general_information.Learning-Teaching Method: a) Giảng dạy trên lớp 30 slotIn class: 30 slots b) Tự học (1h tự học mỗi ngày, luyện tập những kỹ thuật và bài đã được giảng viên hướng dẫn trên Self-study (1 hour of self-study per day, practice techniques and lessons introduced in the course)"c) Tư vấn (trao đổi qua e-mail, trực tiếp …) và tư vấn định kỳ tối thiểu 1 lần/tuần. Chủ yếu trao đổi về các kỹ thuật cơ bản và của bài học, những clip nhạc truyền thống phù hợp với trình độ của sinh viên.Consultation (via email, face-to-face,..): periodic consultation takes place at least 1 time/week, mainly about basic techniques and lessons and traditional music clips appropriate for student's level.
general_information.Time Allocation: Giảng dạy trên lớp 30 slot; 90 phút/slot In class: 30 slots; 90 minutes/slot
general_information.Description: 1. Kiến thức/ Knowledge: - Nắm được những nét đặc trưng về lịch sử phát triển và cấu trúc Đàn Bầu Understand specific characteristics of the historical development and structure of Dan Bau. - Làm quen với nhạc lý và những kỹ thuật cơ bản của Đàn Bầu Familiarize students with music theory and basic techniques of Dan Bau 2. Kỹ năng/ Skills: - Đánh được tối thiểu 3 bài trong đó có 1 bài nhạc nước ngoài ở mức thông dụng vận dụng được đúng các kỹ thuật cơ bản. - Be able to play at least 3 songs including 1 common foreign song and properly apply basic techniques. - Môn học sẽ được triển khai theo đơn vị lớp cỡ khoảng 15 sinh viên/lớp. There will be about 15 students/class. Trong quá trình học, sinh viên sẽ được giới thiệu, hướng dẫn tìm hiểu và thực hành về các nội dung sau: In the course, students will learn: - Lịch sử phát triển của đàn Bầu ở Việt Nam Historical development of Dan Bau in Vietnam - Cấu trúc và đặc điểm của đàn Bầu Structure and characteristics of Dan Bau - Tư thế đánh đàn Postures when playing Dan Bau - Nhạc lý và kỹ thuật cơ bản gồm: Music theory and basic techniques, including: + Gảy dây buông Plucking strings + nhấn lên xuống quãng 2 Raise or lower the pitch to play the major second interval - Luyện tập đánh bài Việt Nam: Cò lả, lý cây đa (hòa tấu) Practice playing Vietnamese songs: Co la, ly cay da (ensemble performance) Bài quốc tế: Auld lang syne dân ca Scotland Foreign songs: Auld lang syne (Scottish folk song) * Sử dụng CNTT trong học phần/ Apply IT in the course a) Cung cấp thông tin, tài nguyên lên mạng : Cung cấp địa chỉ các Website, clip nhạc truyền thống. Update information and resources on the internet: Provide web addresses and traditional music clips. b) Sử dụng các tài nguyên trên mạng: Giảng viên sử dụng có chọn lọc trên nguyên tắc của học phần rồi cung cấp cho sinh viên. Hướng dẫn sinh viên tìm thông tin theo các chủ đề nhất định trên mạng Internet. Use of online resources: Lecturers use resources selectively based on course regulations and then provide them to students. Instruct students to find information on certain topics on the Internet. * Phát triển kỹ năng mềm và phát triển cá nhân trong học phần/ Soft skills development and personal development - Rèn luyện tính kiên trì cho sinh viên, giúp sinh viên tự tin hơn trước đám đông Improve students' perseverance and help them become more confident in front of the crowd " - Phát triển kỹ năng làm việc theo nhóm, kỹ năng hoạt động độc lập của sinh viên thông quan các nhiệm vụ mà giảng viên giao. Develop students' ability to work in groups and work independently through the tasks assigned by the lecturer.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Tham dự tối thiểu 80% thời lượng môn học trở lên để đủ điều kiện thi cuối môn học. Attend at least 80% of class hours to be eligible for the final exam. - Thái độ học tập nghiêm túc. Study seriously. - Ôn tập bài cũ và tìm hiểu tài liệu bài học mới trước khi đến lớp. Review previous lessons and study materials for new lessons in advance. - Luyện tập, thực hành trên lớp và ở nhà. Practice in class and at home. - Tích cực tham gia hoạt động giảng viên yêu cầu trên trong lớp (phát biểu, hỏi đáp, trao đổi, làm việc nhóm, thực hành...) và làm Portfolio cho môn học. Actively participate in class activities required by the lecturer (express ideas, raise questions, discuss, work in groups, practice...) and make a Portfolio for the subject.
general_information.Tools: Nhạc cụ cho từng sinh viên Musical instruments for each student
general_information.Note: Bài tập: 15% Assignment: 15% Điểm ý thức tham gia lớp học: 15% Participation: 15% Thi cuối môn học: Điểm thực hành chơi nhạc cụ theo yêu cầu: 70% (=>4 điểm) Final exam: Playing musical instruments as required: 70% (=>4 points) Tổng điểm FE: =>5 Final Result: >=5

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Hiểu biết cơ bản về lịch sử, sự phát triển hình thành của nền âm nhạc truyền thống Việt Nam. Understand the history and development of Vietnamese traditional music.
Chơi được một số bài cơ bản của nhạc truyền thống Việt Nam và nước ngoài. Be able to play some simple Vietnamese and foreign traditional songs.

schedule.Topic: Phần Lý thuyết/Theory section 1. Tìm hiểu về lịch sử, tên gọi của nhạc cụ Learn about the history and names of the musical instrument 2. Cấu tạo cây đàn Structure of Dan Bau 3. Tư thế ngồi chơi đàn The playing posture 4. Cách gảy đàn (tư thế tay phải, tư thế tay trái) How to pluck strings (posture of right hand, posture of left hand) Phần thực hành/Practice section: 1. Giáo viên làm mẫu kỹ thuật đầu tiên Lecturer models the first technique 2. Hướng dẫn SV cách cầm que đàn, cách tạo ra âm thanh Instruct students how to hold the plectrum and how to produce sounds 3. general_information.Description: In this course, student will build and train neural network, and you will learn the best practices to train and develop test sets and analyze bias/variance for building deep learning applications; be able to use standard neural network techniques such as initialization, L2 and dropout regularization, hyperparameter tuning, batch normalization, and gradient checking; implement and apply a variety of optimization algorithms, such as mini-batch gradient descent, Momentum, RMSprop and Adam, and check for their convergence; and implement a neural network in TensorFlow. Student make extensive use of tools from Linear Algebra, Calculus, Optimization.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose - Promptly access to the https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information

properties.description: In this course, student will build and train neural network, and you will learn the best practices to train and develop test sets and analyze bias/variance for building deep learning applications; be able to use standard neural network techniques such as initialization, L2 and dropout regularization, hyperparameter tuning, batch normalization, and gradient checking; implement and apply a variety of optimization algorithms, such as mini-batch gradient descent, Momentum, RMSprop and Adam, and check for their convergence; and implement a neural network in TensorFlow. Student make extensive use of tools from Linear Algebra, Calculus, Optimization.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Deeply understand the math that makes machine learning algorithms work.

Able to build, train and apply fully connected deep neural networks, implement efficient neural networks, identify key parameters in a neural network's architecture, and apply deep learning to students' own applications.
Able to train and develop test sets, analyze bias/variance for building deep learning applications, apply optimization algorithms, and implement a neural network using TensorFlow.
Understand complex ML settings, diagnose errors in a machine learning system, prioritize strategies for reducing errors, and apply end-to-end learning, transfer learning, and multi-task learning.
Practical project with Tensorflow

general_information.Description: - Knowledge about database systems has become an essential part of an education in computer science because database management has evolved from a specialized computer application to a central component of a modern computing environment. - The content of this course includes aspects of database management basic concepts, database design, database languages, and database-system implementation. Basing on these contents, the course emphasizes on how to organize, maintain and retrieve efficiently data and information from a DBMS.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Promptly access to the https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information

properties.description: - Knowledge about database systems has become an essential part of an education in computer science because database management has evolved from a specialized computer application to a central component of a modern computing environment. - The content of this course includes aspects of database management basic concepts, database design, database languages, and database-system implementation. Basing on these contents, the course emphasizes on how to organize, maintain and retrieve efficiently data and information from a DBMS.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Understand thedatabase concepts and database management system software
Understand the relation model of data and Algebraic Query Language
Understand data normalization and apply normalization techniques in database design
Be able to model an application’s data requirements using conceptual modeling tools like ER diagrams and design database schemas based on the conceptual model.
Be proficient in structure query language including Data Definition Language(DDL) and Data Manipulation Language(DML)
Understand PL/SQL concepts and manipulate with View, Cursors, Stored Procedures, Functions, Database Triggers
Apply the Index in database design and query optimization

general_information.Description: This Course is based on the Coursera Specialization "Business Strategy", which covers both the dynamics and the global aspects of strategic management. Students will learn how to evaluate industry evolution, build and sustain competitive advantage, formulate and assess business strategies, and align efforts to organizational strategy. The course is divided into two parts. In the first part, students will develop their ability to think strategically, analyze the competitive environment, and recommend firm positioning and value creation. The course will explore the underlying theory and frameworks that provide the foundations of a successful business strategy and provide the tools students need to understand that strategy: SWOT, Competitor, Environmental, Five Forces, and Capabilities Analyses, as well as Strategy Maps. In the second part, students will advance their strategic analysis skills, by learning the tools to analyze strategy across time (competitive dynamics), industries (corporate strategy), geographies (international strategy), and institutions (non-market strategy). The course will introduce the tools students need to complete a comprehensive evaluation and understand the strategy dynamics of an industry: Competitive Lifecycle, Internationalization and Stakeholder Analyses, and Diversification Matrices. A key feature of this course is the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) tools and applications, enabling students to generate ideas or structure for their analysis and assist with editing and enhancing clarity while maintaining the student's critical thingking and originality.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose - Promptly access to the FU CMS at http://flm.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Make use of the SWOT, competitor and environmental analysis tools
Assess an industry's structure and how the competitive dynamics in an industry affect profitability
Create a capabilities analysis and apply this analysis in decision making
Analyze the advantages and disadvantages of four generic competitive positions
Define the dynamics of competition, the competitive life cycle, and strategies to survive and thrive through industry disruption
Explain internationalization strategies, how, where and when to enter foreign markets, and foreign direct investment
Explain how businesses compete across industries, the value of being in different markets, and the right degree of diversification
Assess stakeholder management and understand how engaging with non capital stakeholders can create value

general_information.Description: This specialization is designed for those with little or no background in AI, whether you have technology background or not, and does not require any programming skills. It is designed to give you a firm understanding of what is AI, its applications and use cases across various industries. Students will become acquainted with terms like Machine Learning, Deep Learning and Neural Networks. Furthermore, it will familiarize you with IBM Watson AI services that enable any business to quickly and easily employ pre-built AI smarts to their products and solutions. Students will also learn about creating intelligent virtual assistants and how they can be leveraged in different scenarios. By the end of this specialization, learners will have had hands-on interactions with several AI environments and applications, and have built and deployed an AI enabled chatbot on a website – without any coding. Learners will perform several no-code hands-on exercises in each of the three courses. At the end of the last course, learners would have developed, tested, and deployed a Watson AI powered customer service chatbot on a website to delight their clients.

general_information.Description: This six course specialization is designed to prepare you to take the certification examination for IBM AI Enterprise Workflow V1 Data Science Specialist. IBM AI Enterprise Workflow is a comprehensive, end-to-end process that enables data scientists to build AI solutions, starting with business priorities and working through to taking AI into production. The learning aims to elevate the skills of practicing data scientists by explicitly connecting business priorities to technical implementations, connecting machine learning to specialized AI use cases such as visual recognition and NLP, and connecting Python to IBM Cloud technologies. The videos, readings, and case studies in these courses are designed to guide you through your work as a data scientist at a hypothetical streaming media company. Throughout this specialization, the focus will be on the practice of data science in large, modern enterprises. You will be guided through the use of enterprise-class tools on the IBM Cloud, tools that you will use to create, deploy and test machine learning models. Your favorite open source tools, such as Jupyter notebooks and Python libraries will be used extensively for data preparation and building models. Models will be deployed on the IBM Cloud using IBM Watson tooling that works seamlessly with open source tools.

properties.description: This six course specialization is designed to prepare you to take the certification examination for IBM AI Enterprise Workflow V1 Data Science Specialist. IBM AI Enterprise Workflow is a comprehensive, end-to-end process that enables data scientists to build AI solutions, starting with business priorities and working through to taking AI into production. The learning aims to elevate the skills of practicing data scientists by explicitly connecting business priorities to technical implementations, connecting machine learning to specialized AI use cases such as visual recognition and NLP, and connecting Python to IBM Cloud technologies. The videos, readings, and case studies in these courses are designed to guide you through your work as a data scientist at a hypothetical streaming media company. Throughout this specialization, the focus will be on the practice of data science in large, modern enterprises. You will be guided through the use of enterprise-class tools on the IBM Cloud, tools that you will use to create, deploy and test machine learning models. Your favorite open source tools, such as Jupyter notebooks and Python libraries will be used extensively for data preparation and building models. Models will be deployed on the IBM Cloud using IBM Watson tooling that works seamlessly with open source tools.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Learners should be able to describe the business use case and the process of ingesting data.
Learners should be able to use common techniques such as: EDA, visualization, hypothesis testing and statistical tools.
Learners should be able to describe and use common feature selection and feature engineering techniques
Learners should be able to implement the model: machine learning and deep learning algorithms, evaluation and performance metrics.
Learners should be able to deploy the model by interacting with Apache Spark then progressing to a tutorial with Docker.

general_information.Description: The course provides a conceptual framework within which the key financial decisions of the multinational firm can be analyzed. Topics covered include multinational firms and globalisation; foreign direct investment; political risk; foreign exchange markets; currency derivatives (currency options and forward contracts); measuring and managing transaction exposure. Students are required to use AI tools to assist in conducting research, analysing data, and generating content, including making outlines, refining texts, analysing financial dimensions, or creating visual aids.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Discuss the financial operations of a firm within the international environment.
Demonstrate basic understanding of foreign exchange market, exchange rate and currency risk exposure.
Apply key hedging techniques to manage currency risks of international projects.
Demonstrate the ability to produce a clear oral report and/or academic written report, which follows research ethic, that applies understanding of key concepts in international finance.
Practice ability to interract and cooperate effectively with others in the conduct of business.

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN1.1
constructive_questions.Details: How is international financial management different from domestic financial management?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN1.2
constructive_questions.Details: Discuss the major trends that have prevailed in international business during the last two decades.

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN2.1
constructive_questions.Details: Suppose that the pound is pegged to gold at 6 pounds per ounce, whereas the franc is pegged to gold at 12 francs per ounce. This, of course, implies that the equilibrium exchange rate should be two francs per pound. If the current market exchange rate is 2.2 francs per pound, how would you take advantage of this situ- ation? What would be the effect of shipping costs?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN2.2
constructive_questions.Details: Comment on the proposition that the Bretton Woods system was programmed to an eventual demise.

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN2.3
constructive_questions.Details: Explain how special drawing rights (SDRs) are constructed. Also, discuss the cir- cumstances under which the SDRs were created.

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN3.1
constructive_questions.Details: Why would it be useful to examine a country’s balance-of-payments data?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN3.2
constructive_questions.Details: Comment on the following statement: “Since the United States imports more than it exports, it is necessary for the United States to import capital from foreign coun- tries to finance its current account deficits.”

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN3.3
constructive_questions.Details: Discuss the possible strengths and weaknesses of SDRs versus the dollar as the main reserve currency. Do you think the SDR should or could replace the U.S. dollar as the main global reserve currency?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN4.1
constructive_questions.Details: Please answer Problem 1 in the textbook

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN4.2
constructive_questions.Details: Mini Case: Mexico’s Balance-of-Payments Problem

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN4.3
constructive_questions.Details: Mini Case: Mexico’s Balance-of-Payments Problem

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN5.1
constructive_questions.Details: The majority of major corporations are franchised as public corporations. Discuss the key strength and weakness of the “public corporation.” When do you think the public corporation as an organizational form is unsuitable?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN6.1
constructive_questions.Details: Following corporate scandals and failures in the United States and abroad, there has been a growing demand for corporate governance reform. What should be the key objectives of corporate governance reform? What kinds of obstacles can thwart reform efforts?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN6.2
constructive_questions.Details: A CAD/$ bank trader is currently quoting a small figure bid-ask of 35–40, when the rest of the market is trading at CAD1.3436–CAD1.3441. What is implied about the trader’s beliefs by his prices?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN6.3
constructive_questions.Details: Over the past five years, the exchange rate between the British pound and the U.S. dollar, $/£, has changed from about 1.90 to about 1.45. Would you agree that over this five-year period, British goods have become cheaper for buyers in the United States?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN7.1
constructive_questions.Details: Using the American term quotes from Exhibit 5.4, calculate a cross-rate matrix for the euro, Swiss franc, Japanese yen, and British pound so that the resulting trian- gular matrix is similar to the portion above the diagonal in Exhibit 5.6.

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN7.2
constructive_questions.Details: A bank is quoting the following exchange rates against the dollar for the Swiss franc and the Australian dollar: SFr/$ = 1.5960–70 , A$/$ = 1.7225–35. An Australian firm asks the bank for an A$/SFr quote. What cross-rate would the bank quote?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN7.3
constructive_questions.Details: Please answer Problem 12 in the textbook (Part 1)

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN8.1
constructive_questions.Details: Please answer Problem 12 in the textbook (Part 2)

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN8.2
constructive_questions.Details: Discuss the implications of interest rate parity for exchange rate determination.

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN8.3
constructive_questions.Details: Discuss the implications of the deviations from purchasing power parity for coun- tries’ competitive positions in the world market.

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN8.4
constructive_questions.Details: Suppose that the treasurer of IBM has an extra cash reserve of $100,000,000 to invest for six months. The six-month interest rate is 8 percent per annum in the United States and 7 percent per annum in Germany. Currently, the spot exchange rate is €1.01 per dollar and the six-month forward exchange rate is €0.99 per dollar. The treasurer of IBM does not wish to bear any exchange risk. Where should he or she invest to maximize the return?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN9.1
constructive_questions.Details: Please answer Problem 2 in the textbook

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN9.2
constructive_questions.Details: Please answer Problem 3 in the textbook

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN10.1
constructive_questions.Details: Explain the basic differences between the operation of a currency forward market and a futures market.

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN10.2
constructive_questions.Details: Why are most futures positions closed out through a reversing trade rather than held to delivery?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN11.1
constructive_questions.Details: Assume today’s settlement price on a CME EUR futures contract is $1.3140/EUR. You have a short position in one contract. Your performance bond account currently has a balance of $1,700. The next three days’ settlement prices are $1.3126, $1.3133, and $1.3049. Calculate the changes in the performance bond account from daily marking-to-market and the balance of the performance bond account after the third day.

constructive_questions.Details: MINI CASE: The Options Speculator (Part 1)

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN12.1
constructive_questions.Details: Assume that the Japanese yen is trading at a spot price of 92.04 cents per 100 yen. Further assume that the premium of an American call (put) option with a striking price of 93 is 2.10 (2.20) cents. Calculate the intrinsic value and the time value of the call and put options.

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN12.2
constructive_questions.Details: Assume the spot Swiss franc is $0.7000 and the six-month forward rate is $0.6950. What is the minimum price that a six-month American call option with a strik- ing price of $0.6800 should sell for in a rational market? Assume the annualized sixmonth Eurodollar rate is 3.5 percent.

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN14.1
constructive_questions.Details: How would you define transaction exposure? How is it different from economic exposure?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN14.2
constructive_questions.Details: Discuss and compare the costs of hedging by forward contracts and options contracts.

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN14.3
constructive_questions.Details: Should a firm hedge? Why or why not?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN16.1
constructive_questions.Details: Suppose that your company has an equity position in a French firm. Discuss the condition under which dollar/euro exchange rate uncertainty does not constitute exchange exposure for your company.

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN17.1
constructive_questions.Details: General Motors exports cars to Spain, but the strong dollar against the euro hurts sales of GM cars in Spain. In the Spanish market, GM faces competition from Italian and French car makers, such as Fiat and Renault, whose operating curren- cies are the euro. What kind of measures would you recommend so that GM can maintain its market share in Spain?

general_information.Description: This course explores the effect of cultural differences on organisational behaviour and negotiation in the global context. It exposes students to issues and problems that inevitably arise in international business when managers have to deal with culturally determined differences in values, attitudes and behaviours. The course assists students in developing cross-cultural communication competence and management and negotiation skills to successfully solve problems and capitalise on opportunities in a multicultural environment.
general_information.StudentTasks: -Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. -Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments and labs given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time -Use laptop in class only for learning purpose

properties.description: This course explores the effect of cultural differences on organisational behaviour and negotiation in the global context. It exposes students to issues and problems that inevitably arise in international business when managers have to deal with culturally determined differences in values, attitudes and behaviours. The course assists students in developing cross-cultural communication competence and management and negotiation skills to successfully solve problems and capitalise on opportunities in a multicultural environment.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Describe cultural dimensions based on cultural frameworks and apply them to global business settings.
Develop cultural intelligence to interact and manage people from different cultures.
Developing capability to competently apply course concepts in cross- cultural situations that require responses at the individual, managerial and organisational levels.

Identify the major dimensions of culture relevant to work settings and discuss their effect on behavior in an international environment. Describe negotiation styles in different cultures; adjust negotiation tactics to cultural differences.
Explain the motivation, leadership and HR selection across cultures.
Develop cultural sensitivity needed to succeed in any kind of cross-cultural interactions.
Differentiate the different types of negotiation approaches (integrative, distributive negotiations).
Describe the strategies and actions taken on different stages of negotiations; appreciate and explain the importance of pre-; during and post-negotiation phases.
List the roles and functions in negotiation teams; demonstrate the skills of organizing and managing negotiation teams.
Identify different negotiation scenarios, then formulate and apply the instruments of negotiation strategy and tactics.

general_information.Description: This course in an introduction to computer architecture and organization. It will cover topics in both the physical design of the computer (organization) and the logical design of the computer (architecture). The main contents include the organization of a simple stored-program computer: CPU, busses and memory; Instruction sets, machine code, and assembly language; Conventions for assembly language generated by compilers; Floating-point number representation; Hardware organization of simple processors; Address translation and virtual memory; Very introductory examples of input/output devices, interrupt handling and multi-tasking systems. Chapter covered: Computer Evolution and Performance; A Top-Level View of Computer Function and Interconnection; Cache Memory; Internal Memory; External Memory; Input/Output; Operating System Support; Instruction Sets: Characteristics and Functions; Processor Structure and Function; Reduced Instruction Set Computers; Instruction-Level Parallelism and Superscalar Processors; Parallel Processing; Multicore Computers.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact sessions in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises and practical given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time. Do quizzes during class.
general_information.Tools: - Intenet - Textbook - AI Tools and Simulator software

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Explain the general functions and structure of a digital computer
Present an overview of the evolution of computer technology from early digital computers to the latest microprocessors.
Understand the key performance issues that relate to computer design
Describe in detail the essential elements of computer organisation including internal bus, memory, Input/Output ( I/O) organisations and interfacing standards and discuss how these elements function;
Summarize, at a top level, the key functions of an operating system (OS).
Be able to apply Boolean algebra and digital logic to design and interpret complex digital circuits;
Present various types of addressing modes common in instruction sets, an essential characteristics of machine instructions, types of operands supported by typical machine instruction sets
Explain processor structure and function in details, the operations of Reduced Instruction Set Computers
Investigate, evaluate and communicate general trends in computing technologies such as Instruction-Level Parallelism and Superscalar Processors
Using AI tools and simulator tools to futher explore the main concepts

general_information.Description: Introduction to International Business is designed to equip students with a comprehensive understanding of the fundamental principles and practices of conducting business in a globalized economy. It explores the dynamic interplay of socio-cultural, economic, technological, and political-legal factors that shape the international business environment. Students will gain insights into the strategies and techniques for entering and operating in foreign markets, including trade policies, global supply chains, and cross-border management. A key feature of this course is the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) tools and applications, enabling students to analyze international market trends, optimize decision-making processes, and develop innovative solutions to real-world business challenges. By the end of the course, students will be prepared to navigate the complexities of international business with a forward-thinking, technology-driven approach.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose - Read the textbook in advance - Access the course website (www.flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Recognize the key issues of globalization, and the national differences in political, economic, legal systems and culture

Demonstrate understanding about the ethical, corporate social responsibility, and sustainability faced by international business, and explaination how global managers can incorporate such issues into their decision making
Demonstrate understanding about the global trade and investment environment in which international business occurs
Describe characteristics of the foreign exchange market, different theories relating to exchange rate and how to manage foreign exchange risks
Identify the different global strategies and entry modes that firms use to compete in the global marketplace

Explain how firms can perform their key functions including global production, global supply chain management, global marketing, global research and development to compete and succeed in the international business environment
Evaluate external environment of a specific foreign market
Propose the suitable entry mode for a specific company to enter foreign market.
Demonstrate attitude to adapt to differences and complex issues in doing international business
Apply AI to analyze global market trends and consumer sentiment, optimize solutions, and critically address bias, risks, and ethical responsibilities.

general_information.Description: The course is designed to consolidate and enhance students' grammatical knowledge. It aims to achieve this by giving learners exposure to grammar as it is used in real life situations, offering them comprehensive explanations for grammatical forms and meanings, providing contextualized practice of various structures, and developing their use of such structures as well as their critical thinking skills through communicative activities. Students will also be informed of how to recognize common grammatical errors in their written work and encouraged to apply learned grammar in writing. Utilizing a flipped classroom approach, they will engage with core grammar concepts and materials independently before class sessions. They are also encouraged to leverage AI tools as resources to support their grammar learning, practice, and writing processes.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend more than 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Students are responsible to do all exercises and assignments given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptops in class only for learning purposes

properties.description: The course is designed to consolidate and enhance students' grammatical knowledge. It aims to achieve this by giving learners exposure to grammar as it is used in real life situations, offering them comprehensive explanations for grammatical forms and meanings, providing contextualized practice of various structures, and developing their use of such structures as well as their critical thinking skills through communicative activities. Students will also be informed of how to recognize common grammatical errors in their written work and encouraged to apply learned grammar in writing. Utilizing a flipped classroom approach, they will engage with core grammar concepts and materials independently before class sessions. They are also encouraged to leverage AI tools as resources to support their grammar learning, practice, and writing processes.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Analyze how grammar is used in many contexts from a variety of reading and listening texts
Assess whether structures being used are appropriate for written and spoken communication

Compose grammatically accurate spoken and written texts of different topics CLO3.1: Recall basic and advanced structures of English and their meanings CLO3.2: Identify and correct common grammatical errors in both written and spoken English CLO3.3: Explain how and why basic and advanced structures of English are used in different contexts
Proactively collaborate with peers for group work and problem-solving
Critically and ethically use AI tools to support grammar learning.

assessments.Question Type: - From week 3, students work in groups of 5 to: + Choose 2 units from the units taught in the course. + Conduct peer-teaching sessions. For these sessions, they prepare interactive activities to help their classmates review and practice the grammatical structures from the Grammar Notes section of these units . Suggested Peer-Teaching Activities: + Grammar quizzes or “Find the error” challenges + Role-plays or dialogues using the target structure + Mini grammar games (e.g., Kahoot, Jeopardy, sentence race) + Sentence-combining or transformation tasks + Short group writing or storytelling using the grammar point + Peer-correction or editing activities *Students are encouraged to use AI tools to assist with this project. Any use of AI tools must be clearly documented in the project report submitted to the lecturer. Potential uses include: + Generate examples for the target grammar point + Create quiz items, dialogues, or game questions + Get feedback on lesson plans or activity instructions + Other purposes

assessments.Question Type: *Option 1: Students work in a group of 5: - Each group contacts lecturers of ENT/TRS classes, BEN's writing classes (EAW, ERW, ENB) or ENM classes to ask for 3 pieces of writing (paragraphs, essays or emails) in which grammatical errors are largely present. - Each member in a group is in charge of identifying any grammatical errors in the 3 pieces of writing obtained. - Each group writes a booklet for EFL learners. In the booklet, they select the most common grammatical errors (at least 5) from the pieces of writing, put forward suggestions on how to avoid them, and design some exercises to help the readers practice writing sentences/paragraphs with the relevant grammatical structures. - The groups send their booklets to the lecturer in charge for marking and give a presentation on how they have worked on the booklet in class for feedback. - The lecturer in charge can invite other lecturers to come to the class, and the groups can pitch the booklet to them. *Students are encouraged to use AI tools to assist with this project. Any use of AI tools must be clearly documented in the project report submitted to the lecturer. Potential uses include: + Error Identification: Students can first identify grammatical errors manually and then use AI tools to perform the same task. This allows them to compare their own findings with the AI's suggestions. + Researching Explanations: They can use AI tools to find reliable materials that come with grammatical explanations, which will help them write the section on how to avoid common errors. + Designing Exercises: They can use AI tools to generate draft exercises for the booklet, which they must then review and adjust for suitability and accuracy. + Other Purposes. *Option 2: Lecturer’s choice

schedule.Student's Tasks: These activities can be performed throughout Weeks 1–2 so that students can achieve the AI-integration learning outcome by Session 12: - Compare and contrast AI’s explanations to advanced grammatical structures when using different prompting techniques - Compare and contrast AI’s examples when using different prompting techniques Suggested prompting techniques for the activities: + Zero-shot prompting: Give AI a direct, no-example request. + Few-shot prompting: Provide a few examples within the prompt to guide AI on the desired format or style. + One-shot prompting: A specific type of few-shot prompting where only one example is given. + Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting: Break down complex problems into smaller, sequential steps to guide the model through a logical process. + Contextual prompting: Provide extra background information and details to improve AI's understanding. general_information.Syllabus Name: Financial Statement Analysis_Phân tích báo cáo tài chính
general_information.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
general_information.Description: The course provides a framework for interpretation, analysis and evaluation of financial statements from viewpoints of creditors, owners, investment firms and others. Thereby, the users of accounting information understand business strengths or weakness, the impact of general business and specific industry situations, behavior of financial markets, credit or lending criteria, and equity investment standards on present and future company financial conditions. After completing the course, the student shall be able to: - Be familiar with the organization and disclosure of reported information - Quantitatively and qualitatively evaluate core accounting issues that are particularly relevant in the context of financial statement analysis. - Have a framework for forecasting future earnings and financial performance. - Evaluate the business financial performance by applying quantitative and qualitative techniques. - Use financial statement information in a modeling environment to identify and recommend solutions to a variety of financial challenges, and to recommend investment decisions.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by the instructor after class - Use laptop in class only for learning purposes - Read the textbook in advance - Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material on the course, for online support from teachers and other students, and for practicing and assessment.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Apply established techniques, including appropriate technology for analyzing financial statement information for forecasting, valuation, and risk analysis purposes
Integrate and apply the major concepts and theories of fundamental analysis and key steps involved in conducting a fundamental analysis and valuation of a company
Evaluate the impact of financial reporting choices on the quality of accounting information including reported earnings; and assess the quality of accounting information in financial statements.
Use financial statement information in a modeling environment to identify and recommend solutions to a variety of financial challenges
Analyse and synthesise a firm’s financial statement information in the context of the firm’s economic and business condition to make informed recommendations on investment decisions about the firm
Show self-reliance when working independently and collaboratively
Demonstrate ethical awareness and reflection in business context

assessments.Question Type: Exercises, Discussion questions and Constructive questions
assessments.No Question: Depending on the time and schedule of each session.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: All chapters and learning materials covered in each session.
assessments.Grading Guide: Participation grades will be given based on students' preparation, quantity as well as quality of participation in the classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussion, and building upon others’ comments.

assessments.CLO: CLO1, CLO2, CLO3, CLO4, CLO5, CLO6, CLO7
assessments.Question Type: Group problem solving: 15% for group and 15% for individual. Suggestion: Examine and discuss the financial position of 2 entities in the same industry using their financial statements based on a specific investor/ party's view.
assessments.No Question: Problem solving of a comprehensive business event under a 1,500-2,000 word - report
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Thinking creatively, making decisions, solving problems, Personal qualities: Individual responsibility, self-esteem, sociability, self-management, and integrity.
assessments.Note: Students are free to choose the business cases in domestic or abroad.

assessments.Question Type: Problem solving Suggestion 1: Using knowledge so far, introduce an outstanding finance fraud in business and analyze its effect on the financial statements. Suggestion 2: Pick up an article that mentions about the financial situation of any business, figure out the problem and suggest relevant solutions if needed. Suggestion 3: Case study: analyze problems related to practical problems in financial statement analysis
assessments.No Question: Each part includes 1-2 separate problems/ cases

assessments.Note: Students are free to choose the business cases in domestic or abroad or assigned by instructors.

general_information.Description: The AI Capstone Project course is an integrative experience that consolidates the knowledge and skills acquired from the undergraduate AI curriculum into a practical, real-world application. The design of this course challenges students to apply their analytical, problem-solving, and technical skills to solve complex problems using AI technologies. Throughout this course, students will engage with all facets of the AI project development lifecycle, including problem identification, data collection and preprocessing, model design and implementation, evaluation, and deployment. Students will gain a comprehensive understanding of the professional standards and expectations required to successfully execute a project of this nature. This course is structured to be completed by small groups of 3-4 students, fostering collaboration and teamwork. Each group will be assigned a supervisor, who will offer critical support and guidance throughout the research and development process. The supervisor will assist students in refining their project ideas, conducting thorough research, developing and implementing AI solutions, composing a report on their capstone project, and preparing for the final presentation in front of the examination board. By the end of the course, students will have not only deepened their understanding of AI principles and techniques but also demonstrated their ability to apply these concepts effectively in a team-based project. This capstone project not only serves as a significant portfolio piece but also prepares students for professional careers in the field of artificial intelligence.
general_information.StudentTasks: (1) Select a project within the chosen AI concentration: Teams should choose a project that aligns with their interests and the scope of the AI concentration. This may involve identifying a real-world problem that can be addressed with AI solutions. (2) Divide and schedule work: Once the project is chosen, teams should allocate tasks among members based on each individual's strengths and skills. A detailed schedule should be created, outlining milestones and deadlines to ensure timely progress. (3) Attend all scheduled meetings with supervisor: Teams must commit to regular meetings with their assigned supervisor. These sessions are crucial for receiving guidance, discussing progress, resolving any issues, and making necessary adjustments to the project plan. (4) Produce document and product according to project requirements: Teams are expected to produce comprehensive documentation and develop the AI product according to the specified requirements. This includes but is not limited to, designing algorithms, coding, testing, and validating the AI model(s). Documentation should detail the problem, methodology, implementation, results, and conclusions. (5) Present and defend individual contributions in front of the examination board: Each team member must be prepared to present and individually defend their specific contributions to the project in front of the examination board. This includes explaining the rationale behind their approach, the challenges faced, and the solutions implemented. (6) Students are required to attend at least 80% of scheduled meetings with their supervisor(s) to be eligible for the thesis or capstone defense.

assessments.Question Type: Report
assessments.Grading Guide: On-going Assessment (OGA): - Project Introduction (Report 1): 10% - Project Management Plan (Report 2): 10% - Existing systems (Report 3): 10% - Methodology (Report 4): 35% - System Design (Report 5): 20% - Results/Discussion & Conclusion (Report 6 & 7): 15%
assessments.Note: - Require grade >=2 for each part. - Based on the schedule in the syllabus, each group report will be evaluated by the supervisor. This evaluation is called progress assessment. - Individual mark for each progress assessment report is decided by the supervisor and is assessed on the basis of the actual contribution by that individual to the group report. The individual mark can be lower or higher than the group mark and is in the range from 0% to 120% of the group mark where the average score of group members cannot be more than group mark.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: AI, Project management, Research, Teamwork, Presentation
assessments.Grading Guide: - Project Introduction: 5% - Project Management Plan: 5% - Existing Systems: 5% - Methodology: 35% - System Design & Implementation: 20% - Resullts/Discussion & Conclusion: 15% - Presentation Skills: 5% - Q&A: 10%
assessments.Note: - One or more specific members of the student team is not allowed to join the thesis defense (and therefore being failed the subject) if he/she has OGA less than 5. - Capstone project defense mark is given by each member of referee committee for each student on capstone project defense. This personal mark is the average of all member of referee committee. - Each student must make his or her own presentation. - Presentation mark is given by each member of defence committee for each student on final project presentation. Personal mark is the average of all marks given by members of defence committee.

general_information.Description: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed industries around the world, and has the potential to radically alter the field of healthcare. The aim of this unit is to introducethe current and future applications of AI in healthcare with the goal of learning to bring AI technologies into the clinic safely and ethically. Students will be guided to analyze data on patient, such as diseases, medications, tests, or valuable health information, and get a sense of how AI could transform patient care and diagnoses.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Learners should be able to describe the structure of healthcare systems, AI, and machine learning.
The major challenges and the issues in efforts to improve healthcare delivery and system.
How to apply a framework for medical data mining, makes good research questions, and construct a data mining workflow.
Define important relationships between the fields of machine learning, biostatistics, and computer programming.
The machine learning models in dynamic medical practices and discontinuous timelines impact clinical machine learning applications.
Principles and practical considerations for integrating AI into clinical workflows, improving the quality of healthcare applications.
Learners should be able to understand AI-emerging technologies in the fields of healthcare.
The ethical issues for the combination of healthcare system and AI.

general_information.Description: This course is designed based on the Coursera AI for Cybersecurity Specialization by Johns Hopkins University. Students learn to frame cybersecurity problems as data-driven AI tasks, engineer security-relevant features, train and evaluate supervised and unsupervised models, analyze anomalies in network traffic, and assess the robustness of AI systems against adversarial conditions. general_information.Description: This course provides foundational knowledge of machine learning (ML) and AI techniques for solving cybersecurity problems. The content focuses on modeling security challenges as machine learning problems, processing and representing cybersecurity data (system logs, network traffic, security events, endpoint telemetry), and building and evaluating models. This ultimately supports the tracking, monitoring, detection, and prevention of cyber threats to protect data and systems. The module combines theoretical foundations (basic concepts of supervised/unsupervised learning, classification, regression, anomaly detection, model evaluation, overfitting, and ML pipelines) with hands-on Python labs using popular libraries in the cybersecurity domain (such as scikit-learn and introductory deep learning modules). Students will work with real-world cybersecurity datasets applied to tasks such as Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), malware classification, phishing URL/email detection, and user/system behavior anomaly detection. Upon completion of this course, students will be able to: 1. Understand and explain the fundamental concepts of machine learning and how to map them to cybersecurity problems. 2. Design and deploy simple, end-to-end machine learning pipelines: data collection, preprocessing, feature extraction/engineering, training, evaluation, and model improvement for cybersecurity tasks. 3. Apply machine learning techniques to predict attack behaviors, detect vulnerabilities/anomalous activities, and support decision-making in secure system operations. 4. Build a solid foundation for advanced courses in malware analysis, threat hunting, SOC engineering, and AI system security, while gaining practical experience in developing machine learning solutions for digital security.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Understand the Principles of AI/ML/DL Grasp the core concepts, the distinctions between Supervised and Unsupervised Learning, fundamental Neural Network architectures, and the standard workflow for building a foundational machine learning model.
Understand the Cybersecurity Context Comprehend how AI is integrated into security architectures and identify specific cybersecurity challenges that are suitable for AI-driven solutions.

Apply Basic Probability and Statistics Apply fundamental concepts of probability and statistics to model and analyze cybersecurity data, including estimating the likelihood of attack events and evaluating the reliability and statistical significance of detection results.

Apply Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and Feature Engineering Utilize programming tools (Python/Pandas) to collect, explore, and visualize cybersecurity data (such as system logs and network traffic). Execute data preprocessing and feature engineering techniques—including data cleaning, encoding, and feature extraction—to adequately prepare input data for machine learning models.
Apply Supervised and Unsupervised Learning Implement supervised and unsupervised machine learning algorithms to develop models for intrusion detection, malware classification, and anomaly detection.
Apply Deep Learning and NLP for Security Leverage Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to analyze and detect deceptive content, such as phishing and spam, within text and URLs.

Performance Analysis Analyze experimental results using a Confusion Matrix and key performance metrics (Precision, Recall, and F1-score), evaluating the operational impact of False Positives and False Negatives in real-world security environments.
Apply Imbalanced Data Handling Employ data preprocessing techniques, such as resampling and class weighting, to resolve challenges associated with imbalanced datasets.

Analyze AI Risks and Apply LLMs in Cybersecurity Analyze model vulnerabilities, specifically adversarial attacks, and evaluate emerging threats introduced by Generative AI, such as deepfakes and automated social engineering. Furthermore, apply Large Language Models (LLMs) and agentic AI frameworks to address and resolve complex cybersecurity challenges.

Apply Project Development Synthesize acquired knowledge and utilize collaborative teamwork skills to design, implement, and present an end-to-end AI pipeline addressing a real-world cybersecurity problem.

general_information.Description: Giới thiệu/Mô tả môn học: Tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh là kết tinh của truyền thống hàng nghìn năm dựng nước và giữ nước của dân tộc Việt Nam. Trên nền tảng đó, tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh đã gạn lọc các hạt giống trí tuệ của phương Đông, phương Tây, vận dụng sáng tạo và phát triển chủ nghĩa Mác - Lênin vào điều kiện cụ thể của nước ta. Khái quát lại bản chất khoa học này, Đảng ta khẳng định: Tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh là một hệ thống quan điểm toàn diện và sâu sắc về những vấn đề cơ bản của cách mạng Việt Nam, kết quả của sự vận dụng và phát triển sáng tạo chủ nghĩa Mác - Lênin vào điều kiện cụ thể của nước ta, kế thừa và phát triển các giá trị truyền thống tốt đẹp của dân tộc, tiếp thu tinh hoa văn hoá nhân loại. Mục tiêu của tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh là hướng tới giải phóng dân tộc - giải phóng xã hội - giải phóng giai cấp - giải phóng con người. Do đó, tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh là tài sản tinh thần vô cùng to lớn và quý giá của Đảng và dân tộc ta, mãi mãi soi đường cho sự nghiệp cách mạng của nhân dân ta giành thắng lợi. Course Introduction / Description: Ho Chi Minh Ideology is the crystallization of the thousand-year-old traditions of national construction and defense of the Vietnamese people. On that basis, Ho Chi Minh Ideology has selectively absorbed the intellectual quintessence of the East and the West, and creatively applied and developed Marxism-Leninism to the specific conditions of Vietnam. Summarizing this scientific nature, our Party affirms: Ho Chi Minh Ideology is a comprehensive and profound system of views on fundamental issues of the Vietnamese revolution, the result of the creative application and development of Marxism-Leninism to the specific conditions of our country, inheriting and developing the fine traditional values of the nation, and absorbing the cultural quintessence of humanity. Its goal aims at national liberation, social liberation, class liberation, and human liberation. Therefore, Ho Chi Minh Ideology is an immensely large and precious spiritual asset of our Party and nation, forever illuminating the path for our people's revolutionary cause to achieve victory. Mục tiêu môn học: - Về kiến thức: Sinh viên hiểu được những kiến thức cơ bản về khái niệm, nguồn gốc, quá trình hình thành và phát triển tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh; những nội dung cơ bản về tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh; sự vận dụng của Đảng Cộng sản Việt Nam trong cách mạng dân tộc dân chủ nhân dân và trong cách mạng xã hội chủ nghĩa. - Về kỹ năng: Hình thành cho sinh viên khả năng tư duy độc lập, phân tích, đánh giá, vận dụng sáng tạo tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh vào giải quyết các vấn đề trong thực tiễn đời sống, học tập và công tác. - Về thái độ: Sinh viên được nâng cao bản lĩnh chính trị, yêu nước, trung thành với mục tiêu, lý tưởng độc lập dân tộc gắn liền chủ nghĩa xã hội; nhận thức được vai trò, giá trị của tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh đối với Đảng và dân tộc Việt Nam; thấy được trách nhiệm của bản thân trong việc học tập, rèn luyện để góp phần vào xây dựng và bảo vệ Tổ quốc. Course Objectives: - Knowledge: Students understand the basic concepts, origins, formation, and development of Ho Chi Minh Ideology; the core contents of Ho Chi Minh Ideology; and its application by the Communist Party of Vietnam in the people’s democratic revolution and in the socialist revolution. - Skills: Students develop the ability to think independently, analyze, evaluate, and creatively apply Ho Chi Minh Ideology to solve practical problems in daily life, academic work, and professional activities. - Attitudes: Students strengthen political courage and patriotism, remain loyal to the goal and ideal of national independence associated with socialism; recognize the role and value of Ho Chi Minh Ideology for the Party and the Vietnamese nation; and understand their personal responsibility in learning and self-improvement to contribute to national construction and defense. Nội dung môn học: Học phần bao gồm 6 chương, cung cấp cho sinh viên kiến thức cơ bản về Khái niệm, đối tượng, phương pháp nghiên cứu và ý nghĩa học tập môn tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh; Về cơ sở, quá trình hình thành và phát triển tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh; Tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh về: Độc lập dân tộc và chủ nghĩa xã hội; Đảng Cộng sản Việt Nam và Nhà nước của nhân dân, do nhân dân, vì nhân dân; Đại đoàn kết dân tộc và đoàn kết quốc tế; Văn hóa, đạo đức, con người. Content of the course: The course consists of 6 chapters, providing students with basic knowledge on Concept, object of study, research methodology, and significance of studying Ho Chi Minh Ideology; Basis, formation, and development process of Ho Chi Minh Ideology; Ho Chi Minh Ideology on: National independence and socialism; the Communist Party of Vietnam and the State of the people, by the people, for the people; Great national unity and international solidarity; Culture, ethics, and human beings. Phương pháp dạy học: Thuyết giảng và kết hợp trình chiếu các slide bài giảng. Hướng dẫn, giao bài tập đề tài theo nhóm. Tổ chức và hướng dẫn sinh viên thảo luận nhóm, thuyết trình và thực hiện sản phẩm sáng tạo (tham khảo và ứng dụng phần mềm AI một cách có trách nhiệm). Teaching methods: Giving lectures and slide presentations. Guiding and assigning group projects. Organizing and guiding students in group discussions, presentations, and the development of creative products (with the responsible and ethical use of AI tools).
general_information.StudentTasks: Nhiệm vụ của sinh viên: - Tham gia tối thiểu 80% thời lượng môn học và tham dự đủ các buổi lên lớp, thảo luận theo quy định. - Phải có Giáo trình Tư tưởng Hồ Chí Minh (dành cho bậc đại học hệ không chuyên lý luận chính trị) do Bộ Giáo dục và Đào tạo ban hành. - Phải nghiên cứu giáo trình trước, chuẩn bị các ý kiến để đề xuất khi nghe giảng. Chuẩn bị thảo luận và đọc, sưu tầm các tư liệu có liên quan đến nội dung môn học. - Thực hiện đầy đủ các yêu cầu của giảng viên khi học trên lớp cũng như các chủ đề sinh viên tự chuẩn bị trước khi đến lớp. - Chỉ sử dụng máy tính xách tay trong lớp cho mục đích học tập. - Ứng dụng AI một cách có trách nhiệm, đạo đức trong quá trình học tập và thực tiễn. Student's Tasks: - Attend at least 80% of class hours and participate in discussions as required. - Own the Ho Chi Minh's thought (Sửa lại từ sai lệch chính trị "Ho Chi Minh Ideology") textbook (for non-majors in political theory - Nâng cấp học thuật từ cụm "non-politics majored students") issued by the Ministry of Education and Training. - Study the textbook in advance, prepare ideas to propose during lectures. Prepare for discussions and read, collect materials related to the course content. - Fulfill tasks given by the instructor in class as well as topics required to be prepared (Sửa lại ngữ pháp cho chuẩn mực từ cụm "needed to prepare") in advance. - Use laptops in class only for learning purposes. - Apply AI responsibly and ethically in both learning and practice.
